Setup / 7 operator checks

From SSH to the window.

Run each command on the indicated machine. Mark a step only after checking its expected result.

Your checklist0 / 7

Checkmarks record your confirmation. They are not remote test results.

Step 1 / MobaXterm on Windows

Connect with X11 forwarding

Start MobaXterm's X server. Open your Ubuntu SSH session with X11-Forwarding enabled. Keep this original login shell open throughout setup.

Inspect the forwarded display
printf 'DISPLAY=%s\n' "${DISPLAY:-unset}"
What to verify

DISPLAY is populated by SSH, commonly localhost:10.0. The value alone does not prove the connection works.

Do not replace DISPLAY with a Windows IP or use xhost +. If xauth was missing when you connected, install the GUI dependencies and reconnect.
Find the related fix

Step 2 / Original Ubuntu SSH shell

Check the Ubuntu host

Confirm the target release, architecture and interpreter before installing anything. The pinned GUI supports x86_64 on Jammy; ARM64 retains CLI support.

Read the host information
cat /etc/lsb-release
uname -m
python3 --version
What to verify

Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, x86_64 and Python 3.10 or newer. The engine also requires a running systemd instance.

The Qt ARM64 wheel requires glibc 2.39; Ubuntu Jammy uses 2.35. Do not bypass this GUI architecture check.
Find the related fix

Step 3 / Ubuntu SSH shell + MobaXterm SFTP

Deploy the reviewed source

Upload the project ZIP into a new empty staging folder with MobaXterm SFTP. Inspect its file list, then extract into that folder. Run the commands below only when unpacked/shadowsocks-c-manager contains the reviewed project.

Inspect and extract the uploaded ZIP
if ! command -v unzip >/dev/null; then
  sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install --no-install-recommends --no-upgrade unzip
fi
unzip -l shadowsocks-c-manager-0.1.1.zip
unzip -n shadowsocks-c-manager-0.1.1.zip -d unpacked
Install without overwriting an existing destination
if sudo test -e /opt/shadowsocks-c-manager || sudo test -L /opt/shadowsocks-c-manager; then
  printf '%s\n' 'STOP: destination exists; review it first.'
else
  sudo cp -a -- unpacked/shadowsocks-c-manager /opt/shadowsocks-c-manager &&
  sudo chown -R root:root /opt/shadowsocks-c-manager &&
  sudo chmod -R go-w /opt/shadowsocks-c-manager
fi
What to verify

The trusted project is at /opt/shadowsocks-c-manager, owned by root and not writable by other users. Both launch_gui.sh and scripts/setup.sh are present.

Use a new empty extraction folder and a ZIP from the delivered project. Compare its SHA-256 against the delivered sidecar before privileged installation. If the destination exists, review it instead of copying over it.
Find the related fix

Step 4 / Original Ubuntu SSH shell

Install the GUI dependencies

The GUI setup installs missing Ubuntu X11/Qt runtime packages and the pinned Python dependencies in the private project venv. No desktop environment is required.

Prepare the GUI runtime
cd /opt/shadowsocks-c-manager
sudo bash scripts/setup.sh --gui
What to verify

Setup finishes without APT or pip errors and prints the GUI launch instruction. An existing venv is reused only after the privileged installation check.

Read APT and pip failures before retrying. The setup does not alter sshd settings or the firewall. Reconnect SSH if X11 forwarding was unavailable before xauth was installed.
Find the related fix

Step 5 / Original Ubuntu SSH shell

Probe the forwarded display

Run the session probe without sudo. It checks the authority-file location and asks xdpyinfo to authenticate to the display with a timeout.

Check the current X11 session
cd /opt/shadowsocks-c-manager
bash launch_gui.sh --check
What to verify

The launcher reports X11 session: VERIFIED. This confirms the display connection only; Qt loading and administrative workflows are still untested.

The launcher reads XAUTHORITY when set, otherwise the login user's $HOME/.Xauthority. Cookie contents are not printed or copied into a permanent root file.
Find the related fix

Step 6 / Original Ubuntu SSH shell

Open the Ubuntu application

Start the launcher without a preceding sudo. It requests elevation, probes the display again as root, checks the trusted installation and Qt/xcb dependencies, then opens the window in MobaXterm.

Launch the forwarded GUI
cd /opt/shadowsocks-c-manager
bash launch_gui.sh
What to verify

The application window appears on Windows. Its process runs on Ubuntu, with administrative controls and the SSH/X11 display badge.

Keep MobaXterm and the SSH session open. Do not begin from sudo -i: that shell may have lost the original display authorization.
Find the related fix

Step 7 / Ubuntu after installation or migration

Verify the operation you performed

Choose a workflow below and review its result. After a real installation or migration, inspect the service and local listeners. A GUI window or active service alone does not prove proxy connectivity.

Inspect the managed service locally
cd /opt/shadowsocks-c-manager
bash shadowsocks-c-manager.sh diagnose
sudo systemctl status shadowsocks-c-manager.service --no-pager
sudo ss -lntup
What to verify

The reported process and listening protocols match the selected configuration. Complete a real client-side TCP/UDP relay test for the protocols you enabled.

If you only launched the GUI and have not installed a server, an absent managed service is expected. Read journal output locally; do not share configurations or credentials.
Find the related fix

Application / screen example

The application window.

The Fresh installation screen shows server settings, workflow navigation and operation activity. The username has been removed from the title bar for privacy.

Operations / the three modes

Three operator workflows.

The GUI and CLI share the same engine. Review the affected files and service before typing a confirmation.

A new server, with explicit review before changes.

Select Fresh Installation in the GUI. Set a literal listening IP, a port from 1024 to 65535, a password and a reviewed AEAD method. Select tcp_only, tcp_and_udp or udp_only.

  1. The engine rejects an existing or conflicting installation.
  2. The audited development snapshot builds and runs its upstream tests before service installation.
  3. A verified backup precedes managed-file changes; local health checks follow startup.
CLI path for the same workflow
cd /opt/shadowsocks-c-manager
sudo bash shadowsocks-c-manager.sh install
Deliberate confirmationSNAPSHOT · DEPENDENCIES when needed · INSTALL
Review before proceedingSNAPSHOT acknowledges a pinned development revision, not a published stable release. The manager never changes firewall rules.

The existing configuration remains authoritative.

Select Legacy Migration. Discovery must find one active simple server, one JSON source, one port and one reviewed explicit execution command. The replacement is built before the legacy service is stopped.

  1. Password, cipher, endpoint and protocol behavior must map without substitutions.
  2. The original JSON remains byte-for-byte unchanged; a separate target file is generated.
  3. Cutover failures attempt snapshot recovery and verify the restored service before reporting success.
CLI path for the same workflow
cd /opt/shadowsocks-c-manager
sudo bash shadowsocks-c-manager.sh migrate
Deliberate confirmationSNAPSHOT · DEPENDENCIES when needed · MIGRATE
Review before proceedingEnvironmentFile-based defaults, drop-ins, unknown options, stream ciphers and multiple configurations block automated migration. Do not edit a working source just to bypass the checks.

Inspect the recovery point before restoring it.

Create a verified snapshot, list the inventory and select the exact backup you intend to restore. The interactive rollback command lists available backups and asks for their full path.

  1. Every manifest and payload checksum is checked before stopping a service.
  2. Rollback creates a safety snapshot and restores recorded managed files and service state.
  3. Changed legacy evidence is never silently overwritten. Both snapshots are retained.
CLI path for the same workflow
cd /opt/shadowsocks-c-manager
sudo bash shadowsocks-c-manager.sh backup
sudo bash shadowsocks-c-manager.sh list
sudo bash shadowsocks-c-manager.sh rollback
Deliberate confirmationROLLBACK, after reviewing the selected backup
Review before proceedingIf recovery fails, preserve the backup and pending marker. A lost SSH window is not evidence of successful rollback.

Diagnostics / symptoms and next steps

Find the failure.
Choose the next step.

Search the message you see, or filter by stage. Read the cause and the result to verify before retrying.

20 issues

No matching issue. Try a shorter message or select All issues.

X11 displayDISPLAY is unset

What you see

The launcher stops before any window opens.

Likely cause

The SSH session did not establish X11 forwarding, or the environment was changed after login.

Next step

Start MobaXterm's X server, enable X11-Forwarding for the SSH session and reconnect. If xauth was absent, run the GUI setup and reconnect afterwards. Keep the original login shell.

Inspect or retry on Ubuntu
printf 'DISPLAY=%s\n' "${DISPLAY:-unset}"

What to verify

The new session receives its own DISPLAY from SSH. Then run launch_gui.sh --check.

Keep this boundary

Do not invent a DISPLAY value or point it at a Windows IP.

X11 displayXauthority is missing or unreadable

What you see

The launcher cannot read the session authority file.

Likely cause

XAUTHORITY points at a missing file, or sudo -i changed HOME before the launcher resolved the login user's authority.

Next step

Return to the original SSH login shell and reconnect if necessary. If the SSH installation deliberately uses a custom authority file, use its actual existing path in XAUTHORITY. Inspect permissions locally.

Inspect or retry on Ubuntu
printf 'XAUTHORITY=%s\n' "${XAUTHORITY:-$HOME/.Xauthority}"

What to verify

The authority path exists and the unprivileged display probe succeeds.

Keep this boundary

Do not print cookie contents or make the authority file world-readable.

X11 displayThe user probe passes, but root cannot connect

What you see

Launch fails during the second display probe, after sudo.

Likely cause

Root may be unable to read the authority file, including on NFS mounts with root-squash.

Next step

Run launch_gui.sh directly from the login shell so it passes DISPLAY and XAUTHORITY itself. Review authority-file access and storage policy with the server administrator if root is denied.

Inspect or retry on Ubuntu
cd /opt/shadowsocks-c-manager
bash launch_gui.sh --check
bash launch_gui.sh

What to verify

Both probes succeed before Qt starts.

Keep this boundary

Do not use xhost + or copy cookies into a public file.

X11 displayCannot authenticate to the forwarded display

What you see

DISPLAY is set, but xdpyinfo fails or times out.

Likely cause

The X server, SSH tunnel or session authorization is no longer usable.

Next step

Check that the MobaXterm X server is running, then reconnect the SSH session with forwarding enabled. If it still fails, inspect the effective SSH server policy with the administrator.

Inspect or retry on Ubuntu
cd /opt/shadowsocks-c-manager
bash launch_gui.sh --check

What to verify

The launcher explicitly reports the connection as verified.

Keep this boundary

An environment variable alone does not verify X11 access.

Qt & setupQt xcb runtime libraries are missing

What you see

The launcher lists shared library names followed by not found.

Likely cause

The headless Ubuntu installation lacks part of Qt's X11 runtime dependencies.

Next step

Run the GUI setup on Ubuntu and inspect any APT errors. Retry the launcher only after the listed dependencies are available.

Inspect or retry on Ubuntu
cd /opt/shadowsocks-c-manager
sudo bash scripts/setup.sh --gui
bash launch_gui.sh

What to verify

Qt import and xcb dependency checks pass, then the window opens.

Keep this boundary

Do not copy arbitrary shared libraries into the venv or preserve an untrusted QT_PLUGIN_PATH.

Qt & setupQt import fails or the architecture is unsupported

What you see

Setup rejects ARM64, or Qt cannot load on the installed platform.

Likely cause

The pinned x86_64 wheel needs glibc 2.34 or newer. The ARM64 wheel needs 2.39, which Jammy does not provide.

Next step

Verify architecture and glibc. Use the CLI on Jammy ARM64. On the supported x86_64 host, review pip errors and install the pinned GUI requirements through setup.

Inspect or retry on Ubuntu
uname -m
getconf GNU_LIBC_VERSION
python3 --version

What to verify

The GUI target is x86_64 with Python 3.10 or newer on Ubuntu 22.04.5.

Keep this boundary

Do not upgrade the operating system's glibc by hand to force a wheel to load.

PermissionsThe privileged project is not trusted

What you see

The engine rejects source ownership, writable ancestors or unexpected symlinks.

Likely cause

Privileged code or its venv is under a user-writable directory or was copied with unsuitable ownership.

Next step

Review the actual source and every path ancestor. Deploy under /opt/shadowsocks-c-manager as root-owned code. Review any existing venv before reuse; do not change permissions on unrelated directories.

Inspect or retry on Ubuntu
sudo ls -ld /opt /opt/shadowsocks-c-manager
sudo bash /opt/shadowsocks-c-manager/shadowsocks-c-manager.sh --verify-installation

What to verify

The privileged installation check exits successfully.

Keep this boundary

Do not bypass the ownership or symlink guard.

PermissionsThe venv is missing or setup refuses to overwrite it

What you see

The launcher asks you to run setup, or core setup reports an existing environment.

Likely cause

The private environment was not created, is incomplete, or already exists and needs review.

Next step

Use setup.sh --gui for the intended GUI deployment. It can extend an existing environment after verification. Preserve and inspect a broken environment before replacing it; do not blindly delete it.

Inspect or retry on Ubuntu
cd /opt/shadowsocks-c-manager
sudo bash scripts/setup.sh --gui

What to verify

The setup completes, then the launcher imports the pinned Qt package.

Keep this boundary

Do not install dependencies into the system Python or run a user-controlled venv as root.

Qt & setupAPT or pip installation fails

What you see

Package metadata, network access or dependency installation returns an error.

Likely cause

Repository access, proxy configuration, disk space or a package source may be unavailable.

Next step

Read the actual error, check free space and confirm access to the official Ubuntu repositories and PyPI under your network policy. Resolve that cause before rerunning setup.

Inspect or retry on Ubuntu
df -h / /var
cd /opt/shadowsocks-c-manager
sudo bash scripts/setup.sh --gui

What to verify

The complete setup command succeeds; a partial download is not treated as installation success.

Keep this boundary

Do not run third-party repair scripts or perform a blanket package upgrade.

PermissionsAnother manager operation is running

What you see

The single-instance lock cannot be acquired.

Likely cause

Another CLI or GUI engine invocation owns the operation lock.

Next step

Return to that session and review its progress. Wait for completion or use its cancellation flow, then check the reported recovery result before starting another operation.

Inspect or retry on Ubuntu
cd /opt/shadowsocks-c-manager
bash shadowsocks-c-manager.sh diagnose

What to verify

The earlier operation has ended and its final state is understood.

Keep this boundary

Do not delete the lock file or kill an unknown process to force access.

MigrationLegacy environment files or drop-ins are detected

What you see

Migration refuses the default unit, runtime hooks or ambiguous ExecStart.

Likely cause

The automated profile supports only reviewed explicit server invocations. The stock EnvironmentFile-based unit can carry runtime options not represented in JSON.

Next step

Inspect the real unit and effective options locally. An administrator must establish an equivalent explicit instance before retrying; the manager does not make that conversion.

Inspect or retry on Ubuntu
systemctl list-units --all --type=service 'shadowsocks-libev*'

What to verify

One supported explicit service represents the same authoritative configuration.

Keep this boundary

Do not discard DAEMON_ARGS, environment settings or drop-ins just to pass discovery.

MigrationMultiple legacy configurations or ports are found

What you see

Discovery cannot identify one source with one listening port.

Likely cause

The host has multiple server instances, JSON candidates or an unsupported multi-address/port configuration.

Next step

Inventory all instances and their listeners. Use a separately reviewed migration plan for that topology. This release deliberately does not select a source arbitrarily.

Inspect or retry on Ubuntu
systemctl list-units --all --type=service 'shadowsocks-libev*'
sudo ss -lntup

What to verify

The supported single-instance contract is established before cutover.

Keep this boundary

Do not delete working configurations to make the candidate count smaller.

MigrationJSON, cipher or protocol options are incompatible

What you see

Configuration validation reports unsupported or invalid fields.

Likely cause

The conservative profile rejects duplicate keys, arrays, stream ciphers, unknown options and ambiguous semantics.

Next step

Compare the source with the documented supported profile. Preserve the working file and review unsupported settings before considering another migration method.

Inspect or retry on Ubuntu
cd /opt/shadowsocks-c-manager
sudo bash shadowsocks-c-manager.sh migrate

What to verify

Validation accepts every relevant setting without changing credentials, cipher, port or protocol behavior.

Keep this boundary

Do not reformat the original JSON, substitute a cipher or remove unknown fields to bypass validation.

ServiceThe selected TCP or UDP port is occupied

What you see

Installation or cutover stops at the port availability check.

Likely cause

Another process still owns the endpoint, or the legacy service did not release its listener.

Next step

Identify the listener owner and reconcile it with the service you intended to stop. Review the engine's recovery result before trying another cutover.

Inspect or retry on Ubuntu
sudo ss -lntup

What to verify

The expected endpoint is free at cutover and belongs to the correct service after startup.

Keep this boundary

Do not kill a process based only on its port number.

ServiceThe pinned upstream download or build fails

What you see

The build stage exits before the replacement is ready.

Likely cause

The fetch, compiler, bundled dependency validation or upstream test suite failed.

Next step

Inspect the private last-build.log on the Ubuntu host. Resolve the reported cause and confirm that the legacy service remains operational before retrying.

Inspect or retry on Ubuntu
sudo less /var/lib/shadowsocks-c-manager/last-build.log

What to verify

The build and upstream tests complete before any legacy stop.

Keep this boundary

Do not switch to an arbitrary branch or bypass a dependency checksum.

ServiceThe new service fails its health checks

What you see

Startup, process identity, journal or expected socket checks fail.

Likely cause

The actual service state differs from the selected configuration or systemd execution contract.

Next step

Read the engine's recovery outcome first. Inspect the service and journal locally, then resolve the actual cause. Keep both the old installation and the backup.

Inspect or retry on Ubuntu
sudo systemctl status shadowsocks-c-manager.service --no-pager
sudo journalctl -u shadowsocks-c-manager.service -n 60 --no-pager
sudo ss -lntup

What to verify

The expected process and sockets remain present, followed by a client-side relay test.

Keep this boundary

Do not equate active systemd state with successful remote connectivity. Review diagnostic output before sharing it.

RecoveryAn incomplete transaction blocks a new operation

What you see

The manager reports a pending recovery pointer.

Likely cause

An earlier transaction ended without a verified committed or restored state.

Next step

Inspect the pending file locally and list the backups. Review the recorded snapshot and actual service state, then run the rollback workflow when the cause is resolved.

Inspect or retry on Ubuntu
sudo cat /var/lib/shadowsocks-c-manager/pending
cd /opt/shadowsocks-c-manager
sudo bash shadowsocks-c-manager.sh list
sudo bash shadowsocks-c-manager.sh rollback

What to verify

Recovery verifies restored files and services before clearing the pending marker.

Keep this boundary

Do not delete the marker to make a fresh installation proceed.

RecoveryA backup is corrupt or legacy evidence changed

What you see

Integrity or evidence verification refuses restoration.

Likely cause

A payload is missing/changed, the manifest is invalid, or an operator edited the legacy source after the snapshot.

Next step

Retain the rejected backup for diagnosis. Select another verified snapshot, or manually review the source differences with the administrator before recovery.

Inspect or retry on Ubuntu
cd /opt/shadowsocks-c-manager
sudo bash shadowsocks-c-manager.sh list

What to verify

The exact selected backup verifies before any affected service is stopped.

Keep this boundary

Do not recompute checksums to conceal corruption or overwrite an edited legacy file blindly.

RecoverySSH disconnected or the forwarded window disappeared

What you see

The GUI is gone and the operation result is unknown.

Likely cause

The SSH tunnel, X server or Qt process ended. The engine may have continued, stopped or entered recovery.

Next step

Reconnect and inspect the real service state and pending marker before retrying. Use the provider console if network access is affected.

Inspect or retry on Ubuntu
cd /opt/shadowsocks-c-manager
bash shadowsocks-c-manager.sh diagnose
sudo ls -l /var/lib/shadowsocks-c-manager/pending

What to verify

You establish the actual committed or recoverable state using the engine, service and backup evidence.

Keep this boundary

A vanished window does not prove that the operation stopped or rolled back.

RecoveryAutomatic recovery reports FAILED

What you see

The engine cannot verify restoration of the prior working state.

Likely cause

Restoration, systemd reload, enablement or the restored service health check failed.

Next step

Preserve the original and safety snapshots. Keep an independent console open. Review private diagnostics and resolve the failure before deliberately rerunning rollback.

Inspect or retry on Ubuntu
cd /opt/shadowsocks-c-manager
sudo bash shadowsocks-c-manager.sh list
sudo bash shadowsocks-c-manager.sh rollback

What to verify

The engine explicitly verifies restored state. Until then, treat recovery as incomplete.

Keep this boundary

Do not remove either implementation or claim a successful rollback based on file copies alone.

Evidence / read the actual scope

A window is one check.

Application launch, local service health and a successful client relay are different results.

Software test evidence

The software's isolated suite records 87 passing tests and one skipped Unix symlink test. ShellCheck, Ruff and mypy passed.

After an actual install or migration
sudo systemctl status shadowsocks-c-manager.service --no-pager
sudo ss -lntup
Check the process, then the client.

Confirm listener ownership and protocol selection. Test the enabled protocols with a real client. Review local and provider firewalls manually.

Recovery needs evidence.A listening socket does not prove relay. An active unit does not prove connectivity. A disappeared window does not prove rollback.
